our_view.thesis_status: This credit has moved from comfortably compliant to two consecutive quarters of covenant breach, compounded by two separate, confirmed-independent reporting-integrity failures in the same window -- pillars 3 and 4 are graded 'broken' above, not merely 'pressured'. TTM FCCR has declined for five straight quarters: 1.6245x (2025-Q1) -> 1.6099x (Q2) -> 1.6436x (Q3) -> 1.2365x (Q4, the first quarter to fully reflect Amendment 1's 2.00%/month amortization step-up) -> 1.0338x (2026-Q1, BREACH -- WAIVED) -> 0.9192x (2026-Q2, BREACH -- WAIVED). The underlying driver so far looks MECHANICAL rather than purely operational: TTM Covenant EBITDA has actually been broadly stable-to-growing across the same window (~$25.2M at 2024-09 to ~$30.1M at 2026-06, EBITDA margin holding in the ~17-20% range every month checked) -- the deterioration is concentrated in the Fixed Charges denominator (required principal 10x'd by Amendment 1), not a collapse in operating performance. That is a real distinction (this is not (yet) a business in decline) but it does not change the credit fact: the covenant has been breached for two straight quarters, the only relief obtained (the Temporary Limited Waiver) explicitly does NOT deem either test compliant and has now EXPIRED (2026-06-30), and there is no evidence of any new waiver or amendment executed ahead of the September 30, 2026 Test Date -- 15 days from this review. On top of the covenant trajectory, the borrower's own compliance process failed twice in a row: BOTH the March 31 and June 30, 2026 quarterly certificates were originally submitted using a single-month FCCR calculation instead of the agreement-required trailing-twelve-month measurement (caught only by lender query each time), and a SEPARATE March 2026 revenue/cost reclassification error (a $617,841.06 understatement, EBITDA-neutral) was found and corrected in July 2026. Two independent, confirmed-separate correction episodes landing in the same two quarters is a legitimate governance/controls flag in its own right, independent of the FCCR magnitude -- per the standing guidance, this alone would argue against defaulting to watchlist 'off' even if the covenant were compliant.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: Watchlist could move toward 'off'/trajectory toward 'stable' if: (a) new waiver or amendment authority is executed covering the September 30, 2026 Test Date before it arrives, removing the immediate uncovered-breach exposure; (b) TTM Covenant EBITDA growth outpaces the now-stepped-up amortization enough to visibly arrest the five-quarter FCCR decline (even a flattening at 2026-Q3, rather than continued deterioration, would be meaningful); and (c) at least one clean quarterly certificate cycle is delivered with no lender query and no correction notice, evidencing the compliance-preparation process has actually been fixed rather than merely caught twice. Conversely, an unwaived breach at the September 30, 2026 Test Date, a third correction/restatement episode, or a genuine EBITDA decline (as opposed to the amortization-driven denominator effect seen so far) would harden 'deteriorating' further and could warrant escalation beyond routine watchlist monitoring.

business.vertical: Industrial inspection, maintenance, turnaround, and specialist engineering services
business._archetype_note: JUDGMENT CALL: 'services-project' is the closer fit of the three named archetypes -- revenue is billed per project/turnaround with 'project timing, field utilization, mobilization, and customer acceptance' driving monthly volatility (IC Memo), working capital is genuinely collections-led (customer-level AR aging with named 'Collection plan' accounts tracked separately every month), and the company is monitored via 'collections, project-margin, liquidity, and required-principal review' -- all project-services framing, not consumer-inventory (no inventory pledged or tracked) or a fleet-utilization asset-heavy-industrial read. COUNTERPOINT flagged for the analyst: the FY2024 Annual Balance Sheet shows 'Fixed and other assets' of $121,347,780.77 -- fully 77% of total assets ($157,589,224.69) -- which is unusually large for a pure people/project services business and could reflect either genuine owned inspection/testing equipment and facilities, or goodwill/intangibles from the sponsor's acquisition of the business (purchase-price allocation), or both; the annual statement does not break the line down further and the monthly package never reports fixed assets at all. If this balance is substantially operating equipment rather than goodwill, 'asset-heavy-industrial' could be the better-fitting archetype -- flagged for analyst confirmation.
business.business_one_liner: Provides inspection, maintenance, turnaround, and specialist engineering services to asset-intensive industrial customers (refining, chemicals, utilities, pulp/paper, metals, midstream, energy, aggregates, cement, packaging) across four service lines: Inspection, Maintenance, Turnaround, and Engineering.

business_profile.description: Selvara Industrial Services provides inspection, maintenance, turnaround, and specialist engineering services to asset-intensive industrial customers -- refineries, chemical plants, utilities, pulp/paper mills, steel and aggregates producers, midstream and energy operators, and cement/packaging plants. Revenue is earned project-by-project (refinery turnarounds, pipeline integrity work, boiler and tank inspections, plant maintenance, electrical reliability work, shutdown engineering, asset-data programs, safety compliance, and field mobilization), recognized on customer acceptance, with recurring maintenance programs supporting a base level of activity between scheduled turnaround/outage events.

facility._amendment_and_waiver_history: AMENDMENT 1 (executed 2025-10-01, effective 2025-10-05): raised required monthly principal from 0.20% to 2.00% of beginning funded debt (a 10x step-up) beginning the October 2025 payment; explicitly left the 1.2000x FCCR minimum, TTM measurement window, and quarterly Test Dates unchanged. THIS AMENDMENT IS CURRENTLY IN EFFECT (in force since October 2025) and is the primary driver of the FCCR's subsequent decline -- see our_view below. TEMPORARY LIMITED WAIVER (executed 2026-03-20, effective 2026-03-31, EXPIRED 2026-06-30): granted narrow, already-lapsed relief covering ONLY the March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 FCCR Test Dates, explicitly NOT amending the 1.2000x minimum and NOT deeming either test compliant ('BREACH - WAIVED', underlying breach remains reportable, all lender rights reserved). THIS WAIVER HAS EXPIRED and covers no future Test Date -- the next quarterly Test Date (September 30, 2026) is only 15 days after this onboarding review (2026-09-15) and currently has NO waiver or amendment authority in place. A draft waiver-request document exists (Deal Docs/Reference/Waiver_Request_DRAFT_NOT_EXECUTED.pdf) but its own disposition states it is a 'superseded request draft; not legal authority' -- there is no evidence any new relief has been executed for the September 30, 2026 Test Date as of this review.

business._credit_thesis_note: The one-page IC Memo does not itself enumerate discrete thesis 'pillars' -- these four were constructed by monitor-setup from the memo's stated Revenue Model / Downside / Monitoring sections and the credit agreement's own FCCR/reporting mechanics, not copied from an explicit pillar list (same construction method used for Asteron, which also had only a short-form memo). Pillar 3 (covenant protection) is graded 'broken', not merely 'pressured', because the covenant has now been in ACTUAL BREACH for two consecutive quarters (2026-Q1, 2026-Q2) with the only relief obtained (the Temporary Limited Waiver) having already EXPIRED before the next Test Date -- the covenant is not currently doing the protective job it was underwritten to do. Pillar 4 (reporting reliability) is graded 'broken' given TWO independent, confirmed-separate correction episodes landed in the same two quarters (see our_view) -- a materially worse read than a single isolated error. Flagged for analyst review and override -- these are onboarding-assistant judgment calls per the standing instruction not to pause for confirmation on this batch.

transcription_notes: Bare numbers only (per module spec Step 1, transcription not computation): the 'value' field on every test date is the borrower's own stated Calculated/Corrected FCCR, copied exactly as it appears on the cited document -- never re-derived, rounded, or adjusted here.

The certified-values schema carries no field for legal disposition (WAIVED vs COMPLIANT vs BREACH) -- only the bare numeric actual, which the engine compares mechanically to the 1.2000x threshold to produce its own cert_status (pass/breach). That mechanical cert_status will read 'breach' for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, which is mathematically correct (0.9192x and 1.0338x are both below 1.2000x) but does NOT by itself say the breach was WAIVED. The governing disposition for every test date -- 'BREACH — WAIVED (NOT cured)' for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, and that the covering waiver (waiver_1.pdf) EXPIRED 2026-06-30 with NO relief in effect for the next Test Date (2026-09-30, ~15 days from this run's as-of date 2026-09-15) -- is carried verbatim in each quote above and in covenant-spec.json's own 'waiver_status' block (covenants[0].waiver_status, and the top-level covenant_status_alert), which the engine's source_ref already cites for every min_fccr row. This finding is being surfaced directly in this module's conclusion narrative alongside the engine's raw output, since the engine adds no disposition field of its own and none should be hand-added to its JSON.

For 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, TWO figures exist per date: an originally-submitted single-month figure (0.8350x and 0.9133x respectively, both computed in error against the agreement's TTM requirement) and a corrected TTM figure (1.0338x and 0.9192x). Per covenant-spec.json's measurement_window_correction_history and this covenant's window='ttm', ONLY the corrected TTM figures are transcribed here -- the erroneous single-month figures are recorded in this note for context but are NOT entered as certified values, since entering them would reproduce the borrower's own measurement-window error inside this monitoring run.

All 6 quarterly test dates from the covenant's first_test_date (2025-03-31) through the current period (2026-06-30) are transcribed, not only the current period, to let the engine's certified-vs-model cross-check run at every historical test date the model can reach and to preserve the full trend for the memo.

MODEL-VS-CERT VARIANCE AT 2026-06-30, EXPLAINED (engine's own cert_agrees=true / delta_model_vs_cert=+0.014539, within the 0.05 tolerance -- reconciled here to the specific component, not left as an unexplained rounding gap): the model's TTM Covenant EBITDA ties the certificate EXACTLY (30,065,760.56 = 30,065,760.56, zero variance -- the numerator is not the source of the gap). The ENTIRE gap sits in the Fixed_Charges denominator (model 32,199,306.88 vs certified 32,708,421.04, diff 509,114.16) and traces to exactly ONE of its three summed components. Verified line-by-line for every month of the Jul 2025-Jun 2026 TTM window: the model's 'Cash Interest Expense' and 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments' (Balance Sheet tab covenant-support rows, positive-signed, built per covenant-spec.json step7_signoff from the native ledger) tie EXACTLY to the certificate's own TTM Build 'Interest' and 'Principal' columns every month (e.g. Jul 2025: model 1,037,030.12 / 242,695.73 vs cert TTM Build 1,037,030.12 / 242,695.73). The THIRD component, 'Lease payments', is bound by covenant-spec.json's Fixed_Charges formula directly to the borrower's NATIVE Cash-Flow-tab row, which (like that tab's other native lines, e.g. 'Cash interest', 'Required principal') carries an outflow-negative sign convention (e.g. Jul 2025: -18,856.08) -- whereas the certificate's TTM Build lists the same lease amount as a POSITIVE addend (e.g. Jul 2025: +18,856.08). Unlike the interest and principal legs, no positive-signed covenant-support row was built for leases, so the model's literal sum SUBTRACTS lease payments instead of adding them, understating TTM Fixed_Charges by exactly 2x the TTM lease total (2 x 254,557.08 = 509,114.16 -- matches the observed gap to the penny) and correspondingly overstating the model's computed FCCR (0.933739x model vs 0.9192x certified). This is a model/build sign-convention gap on ONE leg of Fixed_Charges, not a dispute over which basis governs -- the model reconstruction still governs the verdict (both sides read BREACH at 2026-06-30 regardless), and the gap is well inside the engine's certified-vs-model tolerance, but it is the full and only explanation for the delta.
